jasmin-arch: Quick follow-up from today's kernel selection sync. we agreed we need a short, prioritized action list to decide Triton vs CUDA/CUTLASS for attention kernels. putting the draft here for review. :spiral_note_pad:

sam-runtime: Thanks. Agree we should separate perf, maintainability, and ops risk. my quick take: Triton wins in iteration speed and custom op expressiveness; CUTLASS/CUDA wins on long-term control and driver stability.

anna-ml: For accuracy/quantization effects we also saw slight fp16 divergence in Triton builds last month. need a reproducible eval harness before we commit.

kevin-eng: Ops questions: driver/kernel binary compatibility across our Dedicated fleet, CI build times, and nightlies. CUTLASS gives a more predictable artifact story for packaging. Triton relies on specific runtime versions.

jasmin-arch: Proposed action items (ranked):
1) benchmarking harness (perf + memory + tail latency) with standardized configs
2) deterministic eval suite (SQuAD-ish subsets + long-context prompts) for quality drift
3) packaging/ops gating matrix (driver, cuda, cuDNN, triton runtime)
4) fallback policy design (model variant + routing)
5) ownership & rollout plan (who does P0/P1 tasks)
6) cost model delta (pricing/throughput numbers)

sam-runtime: I'll take #1 and #4. for #1 i'll assemble a small runner that does steady-state and spike tests. sketch here: 

```bash
# quick runner outline
python bench_runner.py --model t5-xxl --impl triton --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seq-lens 128,1024 --duration 300
```

sam-runtime: Needs a CI job that can run on a gnarly GPU node. tagging @build-bot to add a pipeline.

build-bot: noted. I can provision a nightly job. need a Dockerfile and a small repo. recommended base: nvidia/cuda:12.1-cudnn8 with our runtime libs. :gear:

anna-ml: I'll own #2 (deterministic eval). plan: fixed seeds, pinned tokenizer vocab, and save KV cache snapshots to check for divergence after quant/opt. also will run per-step log-likelihood checks to detect tiny drift.

kevin-eng: I'll lead #3 (packaging matrix) and #6 (cost model), with help from infra. we should map out supported driver versions per Dedicated region. also need an emergency rollback doc if we see perf regressions.

jasmin-arch: good. for #5 ownership: sam=P0 runtime integration + fallback, anna=P0 eval harness, kevin=P0 packaging/canary ops. sara, can you scope SRE coupling?

sara-sre: can do. i'll scope SLO impacts and build a canary checklist (traffic % thresholds, monitoring alerts, automatic rollback triggers). will need hooks from runtime to emit per-request metrics (model impl tag).

sam-runtime: runtime metrics we need: impl=triton|cutlass, kernel-version, seq-len, batch-size, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, memory-alloc failure count. we should add a small structured JSON line per request.

anna-ml: also adding quality hooks: per-prompt perplexity and sample diffs to a small artifact store for quick triage.

kevin-eng: timeline suggestion: two-week sprint for bench + eval harness, then one-week ops integration and canary. so ~3 weeks to initial decision with canary. is that realistic?

jasmin-arch: sounds reasonable. let's commit to sprint goal: "baseline comparison between Triton and CUTLASS (same model/quant) with actionable ops checklist". Owners as listed. due date: +21 days -> last message ts ~1792004820 to reflect end of sprint.

sam-runtime: quick note on implementation complexity: Triton allows python-first kernels, which shortens prototyping, but we must add precompiled fallbacks for Dedicated (so we don't force customers to run Triton runtime). need a binary fallback path in our deployment plan.

kevin-eng: agreed. i'll prototype a packaging layout: /opt/redwood/runtime/{impl}/{version}/lib*. so the node image can host multiple impls side-by-side and we route based on policy.

jasmin-arch: security check: does Triton runtime expand attack surface? @sara-sre any flags here?

sara-sre: surface area higher due to grpc endpoints in Triton. we'll require mTLS between our control plane and runtime, and disallow inbound cluster access. short-term: enforce firewall + mTLS. long-term: consider moving Triton behind our sidecar proxy.

anna-ml: small experimental suggestion: run a toy attention kernel implemented in both Triton and CUTLASS for a few sequence lengths (64/512/2048) to see scaling. i'll attach scripts to the eval harness.

sam-runtime: perfect. i'll add those seq-len sweeps to the bench_runner.

jasmin-arch: ok final ask: each owner pls drop a 1-paragraph plan in this thread by EOD tomorrow with blockers. i'll synthesize into an RFC follow-up with a checklist. :thumbsup:

kevin-eng: will do.

anna-ml: will do.

sam-runtime: will do.

build-bot: pipeline ticket created: CI-7890. nightly runner reserved on infra-staging-gpu1.

jasmin-arch: thanks all. rendezvous in three weeks for canary review.
